comments.body:
Plan-review remediation for 1dd5-1880-17d0-4ac0 (2026-08-21). Every claim below was checked
against the worktree /Users/joeoakhart/impl-2ddd-consolidation. No file was modified.

WHAT WAS FACTUALLY WRONG IN THE ORIGINAL PLAN

1. Two Scope paths do not exist.
   - tests/unit/llm/code_review/test_bugfix_size_gate.py -> no such file. There is no
     tests/unit/llm/ directory at all (`ls tests/unit/llm` -> No such file or directory).
   - tests/unit/plan_review/test_bug_escalation.py -> no such file. tests/unit/plan_review/
     exists but holds eleven other modules, none of them this one.
   The real files are tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py and
   tests/unit/test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py, found with
   `grep -rln "bugfix_size" tests/ src/ scripts/ docs/`.

2. The docs target does not exist. The plan named "docs/plan-review-gate.md (escalation
   section)". `grep -n "escalat" docs/plan-review-gate.md` returns exactly two lines, 497
   ("escalate the" — batch-criteria prose) and 1285 ("de-escalated" — a metrics definition).
   The section this work actually edits is "## The Gerrit bugfix-size attestation gate (code
   review, not claim/close)" at :1058, with related material at "## R4 — the necessity probe +
   the lightweight bug review tier" (:1325).

3. The proposed review-plan mirror would change nothing. The plan said to mirror the repeat-fix
   predicate in orchestrator.bug_blast_radius_escalates so `review-plan` on a bug runs the full
   rubric "under the same condition". Reading src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:191-211,
   that predicate already returns True when a bug's persisted file_impact names ANY non-test
   path. A repeat-fix bug names a non-test path by construction, so it is already escalated. The
   only bugs a mirror could newly escalate are those whose file_impact is empty or entirely test
   paths — and the repeat-fix predicate cannot fire on those either. The mirror is a no-op; the
   corrected plan drops orchestrator.py from Scope and records why in the docs edit so it is not
   re-proposed.

4. Missing consumers. bug_blast_radius_escalates has two call sites, orchestrator.py:245 and
   src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:127. The plan listed neither; workflow_ops.py was
   absent from Scope entirely. Also absent: src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py:202-215, which
   imports bucket_for_verdict / classify_plan_review_attestation / ticket_for_commit_message from
   the gate module by name, and src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:345-347, which calls
   apply_bugfix_size_gate.

5. A pinned test breaks silently. apply_bugfix_size_gate short-circuits at
   bugfix_size_gate.py:262-263 on `non_test <= threshold`, BEFORE any ticket resolution or store
   read, and tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:304
   (test_under_threshold_diff_never_reads_the_store) pins exactly that: it monkeypatches
   ticket_for_commit_message, _load_ticket_state and classify_plan_review_attestation to raise
   AssertionError and asserts `verdict == _verdict()`. The repeat-fix predicate must run on
   under-floor diffs — that is its whole purpose — so this test fails. The corrected plan states
   the rewrite and the narrower invariant that survives, plus the call ordering that keeps
   test_test_only_diff_is_exempt_even_when_huge (:320) passing.

6. The corpus figures are not reproducible by the cited command. The plan said "641 bug-fix
   commits on origin/main since 2026-06-15". scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py has no --since
   option (its argparse offers only --rev-range, --out, --check-planning-corpus), so
   `--rev-range origin/main` walks the whole branch. Running it took ~25 minutes and reported
   644 bug-fix commits, 105 flagged.

7. The label set the recall figures rest on does not exist in the repo, and the ticket does not
   carry it either. AC2 said to compare "to the corpus in this review's scratch data attached to
   the ticket"; `rebar show 1dd5-1880-17d0-4ac0` returns "comments": [] and no attachments. There
   is also no script or artifact anywhere in the tree that computes "this fix later introduced a
   bug". As written that criterion is uncheckable.

8. A hazard the plan did not mention. `--check-planning-corpus`
   (scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py:180-191) asserts the flagged set equals
   ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE exactly and the corpus size equals 113. Folding a repeat-fix verdict
   into the per-commit `flagged` field would break that pinned check. The corrected plan requires
   the new verdict to be a separate field.

WHAT I CORRECTED, AND WITH WHAT

- Replaced the unreproducible label set with one that IS derivable today: the store's `caused_by`
  field, written by rebar.metrics.blame.derive_caused_by on bug close and aggregated by
  rebar.metrics.bug_trends.caused_by_fan_in. That call returns 70 distinct culprit tickets on
  this store right now.
- Re-derived every headline number against that label set (see MEASUREMENTS below) and restated
  them in the plan, with the note that the extended backtest recomputes its own figures so a
  grown corpus reports its own numbers rather than freezing these digits.
- Added the reuse constraint the parent epic implies. Epic 2ddd-b523-06da-4b4a is "Collapse
  duplicated logic into shared modules", and commit->ticket resolution already exists twice:
  bugfix_size_gate.ticket_for_commit_message (bugfix_size_gate.py:138-151) and
  metrics/blame._commit_ticket (src/rebar/metrics/blame.py:171), both wrapping
  rebar._commands.verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs +
  rebar._engine_support.resolver.resolve_ticket_id. The new module calls the former instead of
  adding a third copy.
- Recorded the monkeypatch-by-string surface (test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:210-224 and
  :308-310, all without raising=False) so the new predicate is reachable as a module-level name
  in bugfix_size_gate and the existing patching style still neutralises it.
- Recorded the two ratchets rather than leaving them to surprise the implementer:
  apply_bugfix_size_gate scores C901 9 against the max-complexity 15 ceiling, and
  bugfix_size_gate.py is 322 lines against the 800 module cap.
- Rewrote every acceptance criterion as a command with its current-tree result, so each fails on
  main today and passes after a correct implementation. The two criteria that pass today
  (--check-planning-corpus, and the existing ad0d test files) are labelled as pinning criteria
  rather than left to read as vacuous checks.

CLAIMS THAT SURVIVED VERIFICATION UNCHANGED

- bugfix_size_gate.py:42 really is BUGFIX_SIZE_THRESHOLD_NON_TEST_LINES = 150.
- The plan's citation of orchestrator.py:191-211 for bug_blast_radius_escalates is exact.
- extract_ticket_refs really lives at rebar._commands.verify_commit.
- 8d862d1058 is real and is a bug fix: `git log -1` gives subject "7084: resolve a ticket's
  commits in ONE git walk", `rebar show 7084` gives ticket_type "bug"
  (7084-4e33-e698-42dd, closed), and count_non_test_diff_lines over `git show 8d862d1058
  --format=` returns exactly 127 — under the 150 floor, which is the point.

MEASUREMENTS

Command 1 — the corpus:
  python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range origin/main --out /tmp/bt_full.json
  -> bug-fix commits: 644; flagged (> 150 non-test lines): 105
  -> rev_range "origin/main", corpus_rule "gate:trailer-or-subject"
  -> per-commit keys emitted today: commit, flagged, non_test_lines, ticket
  (Two "Ambiguous prefix 'dc33' matches multiple tickets" lines appear on stderr; the resolver
  refuses ambiguous 4-digit prefixes and the script skips those commits.)

Command 2 — the label set:
  rebar.metrics.bug_trends.caused_by_fan_in('.') -> 70 culprit tickets
  Intersected with the 644-commit corpus: 22 commits name a recorded culprit.
  Of those 22, 10 are flagged by the 150-line floor.
  Whole-corpus escalation rate for the floor: 105/644 = 16.3%.

Command 3 — the repeat-fix rule, implemented ad hoc exactly as the plan describes (>=2 prior
bug-fix commits touching the same non-test file within 7 days, over one
`git log --no-merges --format=... --name-only origin/main` pass, non-test classification via
bugfix_size_gate.is_test_path):
  repeat-fix escalated: 224 of 644 = 34.8%
  labelled commits caught by repeat-fix: 12 of 22
  labelled commits caught by the 150-line floor: 10 of 22
  labelled commits caught by either: 14 of 22
  union escalation rate: 251 of 644 = 39.0%

So the plan's direction is sound and its shape was right — the original "17 of 29 at 37%
escalation" is very close to the reproducible "12 of 22 at 34.8%". Only the denominator was
unreproducible, and that is what the corrected plan fixes.

Command 4 — complexity headroom:
  ruff check --select C901 src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py -> All checks passed
  ruff check --select C901 --config lint.mccabe.max-complexity=1 -> apply_bugfix_size_gate is 9,
  classify_plan_review_attestation 7, count_non_test_diff_lines 8.

comments.body:
Plan verified against the tree before implementing. Every factual claim held (only line-number drift: `derive_caused_by` is at blame.py:184 not :171; the two pinned tests are at test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:323/:339 not :304/:320; the docs section starts at plan-review-gate.md:1060 not :1058). The 'review-plan mirror is a no-op' constraint checks out: `bug_blast_radius_escalates` returns True for any non-test path in `file_impact`.

Two ACs did NOT hold as written and were corrected:

1. AC1's unanchored `grep -c` prints 7, not 3 — it counts the definitions plus their in-module uses. Anchored to `^` it prints 3, which is what the criterion meant.
2. AC7 (`--check-planning-corpus` exits 0) fails on current `origin/main`: `corpus=114 (want 113); missed=[]; mechanical_fp=[]; FAIL`. Reproduced unchanged on a pristine detached worktree at `origin/main`, so it is pre-existing, not caused by this change — filed as bug 648b-7882-497f-45fc (grateful-electronic-vaquita) and linked `discovered_from`. The half of the check this AC actually pins — that `flagged` still means the size floor alone — passes: `missed=[]`, `mechanical_fp=[]`.

Backtest re-measured on today's `origin/main` (645 bug-fix commits, 24 labelled from `caused_by`):

| predicate | recall | escalation |
|---|---|---|
| size (floor) | 10/24 (41.7%) | 105/645 (16.3%) |
| repeat-fix | 12/24 (50.0%) | 227/645 (35.2%) |
| union | 14/24 (58.3%) | 253/645 (39.2%) |

The floor row reconciles exactly with the plan's measurement (105 flagged at 16.3%); the plan saw 644 commits and 22 labels, today 645 and 24. Repeat-fix recall and escalation land within a point of the planned figures.

comments.body:
Implementation landed as Gerrit change 2079 (patchset 2).

Mutation evidence — every new test was verified by perturbing the live implementation and confirming a specific test goes RED, then restoring:

| mutation | test that caught it |
|---|---|
| drop `--no-merges` from the log walk | `test_merge_commits_are_not_counted_as_prior_fixes` (3 != 2) |
| `REPEAT_FIX_MIN_PRIOR` 2 -> 1 | `test_a_single_prior_bug_fix_does_not_escalate` |
| `REPEAT_FIX_WINDOW_DAYS` 7 -> 70 | `test_prior_bug_fixes_outside_the_window_do_not_escalate` |
| count any resolvable ticket, not only `bug` | `test_prior_commits_on_a_non_bug_ticket_do_not_escalate` |
| tally priors across paths instead of per path | `test_priors_are_counted_per_path_not_across_paths` |
| ignore the `at` anchor (always "now") | `test_at_pins_the_window_to_a_point_in_time` |
| drop the repeat-fix arm of the OR | 4 gate tests incl. `test_both_signals_are_reported_together` |
| `non_test_paths_in_diff` keeps test paths | `test_non_test_paths_in_diff_drops_test_material` |
| blank `repeat_fix_priors` in coverage | `test_repeat_fix_escalates_an_under_floor_bug_fix` |
| teaching finding drops the priors clause | `test_the_teaching_finding_names_the_prior_fixes` |
| walk `HEAD` instead of `HEAD~1` | `test_the_change_under_review_is_not_counted_as_its_own_prior` |

The last one was a genuine defect found while implementing, not just a mutation: `assemble` builds the review diff as `HEAD~1..HEAD`, so in a review checkout HEAD IS the change under review. A first draft walked `HEAD`, which would have let a fix with a single genuine prior count itself as the second one and escalate on its own existence. Fixed by walking `HEAD~1` (the same base the diff is taken against) and pinned by the regression test above.

Ratchets: module-size 143 lines for the new module, `bugfix_size_gate.py` 392 of 800; `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:42` sets `BUGFIX_SIZE_THRESHOLD_NON_TEST_LINES = 150`. On Gerrit only, a change whose trailer resolves to a `bug` and whose diff exceeds 150 non-test lines must carry an acceptable plan-review attestation or the bot votes `LLM-Review -1` (`bugfix_size_gate.py:248-322`; docs `docs/plan-review-gate.md:1058`). A fix at or under the floor is never asked for a plan.

Measured by `python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range origin/main` (all of `origin/main`):

- 644 bug-fix commits; 105 over the floor = 16.3% escalation.
- "This fix later introduced a bug" is labellable from the store's `caused_by` field (aggregated by `bug_trends.caused_by_fan_in`): 22 of the 644 name one.
- Size floor catches 10 of 22. Repeat-fix signal (a non-test file touched by >=2 other bug-fix commits on the base branch in the prior 7 days) catches 12 of 22 at 34.8% escalation (224/644). Union: 14 of 22 at 39.0%.
- Under the floor today: `8d862d1058` (bug `7084-4e33-e698-42dd`) is 127 non-test lines.

Pure git history plus ticket type — no path lists, no CI provider required (portability).

## Approach
New module `src/rebar/llm/code_review/repeat_fix.py`: `REPEAT_FIX_WINDOW_DAYS = 7`, `REPEAT_FIX_MIN_PRIOR = 2`, `repeat_fix_escalates(paths, *, repo_root, base_ref, at) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]` (verdict + the priors the teaching finding names). Per non-test path it walks `git log --no-merges --since/--until <path>` on the base branch, counting commits whose message resolves to a `bug` ticket.

`apply_bugfix_size_gate` gains this order, which preserves the other pinned exemptions: (1) extract non-test paths, empty -> return with no reads; (2) escalate if `non_test_lines > 150` OR `repeat_fix_escalates(...)`, else return; (3) resolve ticket, require `ticket_type == "bug"`, classify attestation — unchanged.

## Constraints
- **The `review-plan` mirror is a no-op; NOT in scope.** `orchestrator.bug_blast_radius_escalates` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:191-211`) already returns True for a bug whose `file_impact` names ANY non-test path, which every repeat-fix bug does. The only bugs a mirror could newly escalate have empty/test-only `file_impact`, where the predicate cannot fire either. Its call sites `orchestrator.py:245` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:127` stay unchanged; the docs edit records this so it is not re-proposed.
- **A pinned invariant changes deliberately.** `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:304` (`test_under_threshold_diff_never_reads_the_store`) patches `ticket_for_commit_message`, `_load_ticket_state`, `classify_plan_review_attestation` to raise and asserts an under-floor diff leaves the verdict untouched — but the predicate must run on under-floor diffs. Rewrite it to the surviving invariant: an under-floor diff with no non-test files, or no repeat-fix hit, performs no attestation classification. `test_test_only_diff_is_exempt_even_when_huge` (`:320`) must pass unchanged.
- **`flagged` keeps meaning the size floor alone.** `--check-planning-corpus` (`scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py:180-191`) asserts the flagged set equals `ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE` exactly, so the repeat-fix verdict is a NEW field beside `flagged`, never folded into it.
- **Additive coverage keys only.** `coverage["bugfix_size_gate"]` gains `escalation_reason` (`size`/`repeat-fix`/`size+repeat-fix`) and `repeat_fix_priors` as NEW keys, so the consumers need no edit: `src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py:202-215` (imports `bucket_for_verdict`, `classify_plan_review_attestation`, `ticket_for_commit_message` by name) and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:345-347`.
- **Reuse the resolver.** Commit->ticket resolution exists at `bugfix_size_gate.py:138-151` and `metrics/blame.py:171`; call the former, do not add a third copy.
- **Patchable by name.** Reach the predicate through a module-level name in `bugfix_size_gate`, so the existing string-keyed `monkeypatch.setattr(bsg, "<name>", ...)` sites (`test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:210-224`, `:308-310`, no `raising=False`) can neutralise it.
- **Ratchets / fail-open.** `apply_bugfix_size_gate` scores C901 9 of 15 and the module is 322 of 800 lines, so extract the predicate evaluation into a helper. A git failure yields no escalation and no exception.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/repeat_fix.py` (new); `bugfix_size_gate.py`; `scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py` (add `--repeat-fix` and `--labels-from-caused-by`, importing the shipped predicate so the script cannot drift); `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (the section at `:1058` — there is no "escalation section" in that file); `tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py`; `tests/unit/test_bugfix_repeat_fix_1dd5.py` (new).

Reviewed, NOT changed: `orchestrator.py`, `workflow_ops.py`, `review_bot/retrigger.py`, `code_review/finalize.py`, `metrics/blame.py`.

## Testing
Fixture repo built in-test, not this repo's history. Escalates: two prior bug-trailer commits inside 7 days on a 20-line fix. Does not: one prior fix; two 8 days back; priors resolving to a non-bug ticket or to nothing; merge commits; a test-only diff (which also reads nothing). The floor still escalates alone; a git failure fails open.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Predicate + parameters ship in their own module. `grep -c "^REPEAT_FIX_WINDOW_DAYS\|^REPEAT_FIX_MIN_PRIOR\|^def repeat_fix_escalates" src/rebar/llm/code_review/repeat_fix.py` prints `3` (anchored to the three DEFINITIONS; unanchored also counts their uses). Today the file is absent (exit 2).
- [ ] New unit tests pass. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_repeat_fix_1dd5.py -q` exits 0. Today pytest exits 4.
- [ ] An under-floor repeat-fix is escalated. `tests/unit/test_bugfix_repeat_fix_1dd5.py::test_repeat_fix_escalates_an_under_floor_bug_fix` asserts `verdict["coverage"]["bugfix_size_gate"]["escalation_reason"] == "repeat-fix"`. Today an under-floor diff writes no `coverage` entry (`bugfix_size_gate.py:262-263`).
- [ ] Existing gate behaviour preserved. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py tests/unit/test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py -q` exits 0 (pinning; passes today, with the one test rewritten as above).
- [ ] Backtest emits the repeat-fix verdict from the shipped predicate. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range HEAD~200..HEAD --repeat-fix --out /tmp/bt.json` exits 0 and `python -c "import json; c=json.load(open('/tmp/bt.json'))['commits']; assert c and all('repeat_fix' in r for r in c)"` exits 0. Today `--repeat-fix` is unrecognised (exit 2) and rows carry only `commit`/`ticket`/`non_test_lines`/`flagged`.
- [ ] Backtest labels from the store and reports recall per predicate. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --rev-range origin/main --repeat-fix --labels-from-caused-by --out /tmp/bt_full.json` exits 0 and prints labelled-recall + escalation rate per predicate (2026-08-21: 22 labelled; floor 10/22 at 16.3%, repeat-fix 12/22 at 34.8%, union 14/22 at 39.0%). Today `--labels-from-caused-by` is unrecognised (exit 2). The command recomputes its own figures, so the criterion is that the summary exists and its floor row reconciles, not that the digits are frozen.
- [ ] `flagged` still means the floor alone. `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --check-planning-corpus` reports `missed=[]; mechanical_fp=[]` — the flagged set is still exactly `ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE`, which is the guard. Its other arm, `corpus=114 (want 113)` (exit 1), is a PRE-EXISTING drift reproduced unchanged on pristine `origin/main`; tracked separately, out of scope.
- [ ] Docs record the predicate and why `review-plan` is not mirrored. `grep -c "repeat-fix" docs/plan-review-gate.md` prints >= `2`. Today `0`.
compiled_state.title: Escalate repeat fixes to plan review: a file bug-fixed twice in the prior 7 days
